One day out on the Plainfield, he came across a panicked middle-aged man and, not far off, an old woman lying in a wheat field, barely hanging on. 
They didn't ask for medicine—he could see, and so could the man, that there was no saving her. 
The man asked him for some paper and a brush, but he only had a scrap of cloth in his pack. The old woman took it and, with shaky hands, drew out a recipe. She was already fading, her mind clouded, mumbling over and over about leaving a bowl of noodles for her son back home. As she wrote, her tears soaked the cloth, smearing the charcoal marks. It was a hard, painful farewell. She clearly didn't want to let go. 
He realized it was a recipe for locust leaf noodles.

I am aware of the injustices you have suffered in the Jianghu.
The Way of the Silver Needle is this: a price for a life. When those in the Jianghu promise payment to a disciple of our sect, they must have the courage to honor it. From this day forward, if any of you provide treatment and the patient breaks their promise of reward, you are to place a bounty upon their head. Let all heroes in the Jianghu hunt down such faithless wretches. And if you ask for mere praise and are still met with scorn... then I shall personally meet with those cowards and claim justice for you.
